<?php

/**
 * F-457 FIXTURE — the ways a PeepSo model write used to walk past the guard.
 *
 * NOT loadable code and never scanned as part of the tree: it lives under
 * tests/fixtures/ with a .txt suffix so neither the guard's own roots nor
 * PHP's autoloader can see it. The guard is pointed at this file explicitly.
 *
 * ⛔ None of these constructs exists in bcc-core or bcc-trust today. That is
 * precisely why a fixture is the only way to test the rules that forbid
 * them — there is nothing in either tree for them to catch, so without this
 * file the deny rules would be green and unexercised.
 *
 * Every write below MUST be reported, and reported UNPINNED.
 */

namespace Fixture\Dodged;

use PeepSoGroup as Community;          // an ALIASED import
use PeepSoGroup as GroupAlias;

class DodgesTheNameMatch
{
    /** 1. An `->update(` on a receiver no pre-pass could tie to a literal new. */
    public function updateThroughAProperty(): void
    {
        $this->group->update(['owner_id' => 7]);
    }

    /** 2. An `->update(` on a receiver returned by a method. */
    public function updateThroughAMethodReturn(): void
    {
        $group = $this->resolveGroup();
        $group->update(['owner_id' => 7]);
    }

    /** 3. The same spelling on $wpdb, which is NOT a model write. */
    public function updateOnWpdbIsNotAModelWrite(): void
    {
        global $wpdb;
        $wpdb->update('wp_posts', ['post_title' => 'x'], ['ID' => 1]);
    }

    /**
     * 3b. The PHP 8 NULLSAFE operator. `?->` is its OWN token
     * (T_NULLSAFE_OBJECT_OPERATOR), so a rule that only knew
     * T_OBJECT_OPERATOR let this past entirely.
     */
    public function updateThroughANullsafeOperator(): void
    {
        $this->group?->update(['owner_id' => 7]);
    }

    /** 3c. And the same spelling on $wpdb is still not a model write. */
    public function nullsafeUpdateOnWpdbIsNotAModelWrite(): void
    {
        global $wpdb;
        $wpdb?->update('wp_posts', ['post_title' => 'x'], ['ID' => 1]);
    }

    /** 4. A DYNAMIC new: the class name is in a variable. */
    public function dynamicNew(string $cls, array $data): void
    {
        $group = new $cls(null, $data);
    }

    /** 5. An ALIASED import of the model class. */
    public function aliasedNew(array $data): void
    {
        $group = new Community(null, $data);
    }

    /** 6. A SUBCLASS of the model class. */
    public function subclassNew(array $data): void
    {
        $group = new GatedCommunity(null, $data);
    }

    /** 7. A `[$obj, 'update']` callable, so the name never appears as a call. */
    public function callableUpdate(): void
    {
        $fn = [$this->group, 'update'];
        $fn(['owner_id' => 7]);
    }
}

/**
 * 8. A subclass declaration, which is how #6 becomes possible.
 *
 * ⚠ TWO forms on purpose. The ALIASED parent is caught by the
 * aliased-import rule, not by the subclass rule — the alias name carries
 * no trace of the model. Only the DIRECT form exercises `extends`, so
 * both are here and the layering is visible.
 */
class GatedCommunity extends GroupAlias
{
}

class DirectlyGatedCommunity extends \PeepSoGroup
{
}

/** 9. class_alias, the runtime version of an aliased import. */
class_alias('PeepSoGroup', 'FixtureGroupAlias');
